decisions.difference: A: (finding Facial swelling)  vs  B: (finding Swelling (finding_site Face structure))
decisions.reason: The page says "swelling of face" and SNOMED has a precoordinated concept with exactly that meaning; B's post-coordinated form says the same thing less directly.

decisions.difference: A: (finding Swelling (finding_site Tooth, gum, and/or supporting structure))  vs  B: (finding Swollen gums)
decisions.final_expr: (finding (snomed_concept "Clinical finding" "finding") (snomed_concept "Swelling" "finding") (attribute (snomed_concept "Finding site" "attribute") (snomed_concept "Tooth, gum, and/or supporting structure" "body structure")))
decisions.reason: "Swelling next to tooth" names the tissue around the tooth, not only the gums; A's site covers gum and supporting structures and still includes Swollen gums as a descendant.

decisions.difference: A: (finding Tooth absent)  vs  B: (finding Tooth loss)
decisions.reason: The page says "missing teeth", and "missing tooth" is a SNOMED synonym of Tooth absent; Tooth loss describes the process of losing a tooth, not the observed state.

decisions.difference: A: (and Toothache Pus@Oral cavity Swelling@Tooth/gum)  vs  B: (and Toothache (or Pus@Oral cavity Swollen gums))
decisions.final_expr: (and Toothache Pus@Oral cavity structure Swelling@Tooth, gum, and/or supporting structure)
decisions.reason: "Previous/current tooth pain with pus in mouth, swelling next to tooth" lists the features with no "or" (other boxes on this page write "or" when they mean it), so the literal reading is all three; the page doesn't rule out the either/or reading.
